_metadata.description: Physically measured constants for Minecraft solid material blocks. For use in PBR rendering pipeline.

sources.f0_f82: Computed from complex IOR via Fresnel equations. Adobe Standard Material references for cross-validation.
sources.physical_properties: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, Engineering Toolbox, WebMineral, Mindat.org
sources.sss: Jensen et al. 2001 (marble). Other materials estimated from absorption spectra.
sources.dispersion: Schott Glass Catalog, Sellmeier coefficients from refractiveindex.info
sources.wood: Forest Products Laboratory Wood Handbook (USDA FPL-GTR-190)

notes.f0_computation: F0 = ((n-1)^2 + k^2) / ((n+1)^2 + k^2) for metals; ((n-1)/(n+1))^2 for dielectrics
notes.roughness_values: Artistic estimates based on real-world surface finish. 0.0 = perfect mirror, 1.0 = fully diffuse
notes.fictional_materials: Marked with is_fictional=true. Suggested real-world analogues provided where possible.
notes.ior_note: For metals, IOR is complex (n+ik). For dielectrics, only real part n is significant (k≈0).
notes.sss_units: sigma_s_prime and sigma_a in mm^-1 per RGB channel (reduced scattering and absorption coefficients)

emission.note: Non-emissive at room temperature. Emissivity for thermal radiation reference.
Extremely low emissivity — excellent IR reflector.
Polished copper. Oxidized copper emissivity rises to 0.6-0.8.

thin_film.note: Copper oxide patina (Cu2O) forms naturally. Film IOR ~2.7, thickness 50-200nm.

complex_ior.source: Tungsten (W) from Ordal et al. 1988 — used as analogue

physical.note: Based on tungsten. Netherite is fictional — highest melting point metal used as analogue.

optical.note: Cinnabar has extremely high IOR for a non-metal. Deep red color from HgS bandgap.

subsurface.note: Cinnabar is somewhat translucent in thin sections with deep red color.

emission.note: Redstone glows faintly red — purely fictional property.

dispersion.note: Cinnabar has extreme dispersion (high birefringence too).

ancient_debris.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Dense iron-gold alloy or meteoritic iron

physical.note: Estimated. Ancient debris is fire-resistant and extremely dense in-game.

optical.note: Highest IOR of any common natural gemstone. Very high F0 for a dielectric.

transmission.note: Type IIa diamond is optically transparent across entire visible spectrum.

sellmeier_coefficients.note: Diamond's strong dispersion creates 'fire' in cut gems.

birefringence.note: Cubic crystal system — optically isotropic, no birefringence.

physical.note: Highest thermal conductivity of any natural material. Sublimes rather than melts at 1atm.

subsurface.note: Green color from Cr3+ absorption bands at 600nm and 430nm. Transmits 500-550nm (green).

transmission.note: Most emeralds have inclusions ('jardin') reducing clarity. Ideal emerald transmits green.

subsurface.note: Purple from Fe3+/Fe4+ charge transfer. Absorbs green-yellow (550nm), transmits red+blue.

optical.note: Deep blue from S3- radical ion trapped in sodalite cage structure.

subsurface.note: Opaque but can show slight translucency at thin edges. Deep blue absorption.
Milky quartz has micro-inclusions causing strong scattering. Clear quartz has minimal SSS.

transmission.note: Pure quartz is highly transparent. Milky quartz is translucent.

optical.note: Black color from magnetite (Fe3O4) nanocrystals dispersed in glass matrix.

surface.note: Conchoidal fracture produces atomically smooth surfaces. Can be polished to near-perfect mirror.

transmission.note: Extremely thin sections (< 1mm) show dark brown/red transmission.

birefringence.note: Amorphous glass — no crystal structure, no birefringence.

crying_obsidian.real_world_material: Fictional — obsidian with luminous purple inclusions

emission.note: Purple glowing tears — fictional emissive property.

optical.note: Very high birefringence — famous for double-image (Iceland spar).

subsurface.note: SSS values from Jensen 2001 marble measurements (marble ≈ metamorphosed calcite).

transmission.note: Clear calcite (Iceland spar) is highly transparent. Massive calcite is translucent.

birefringence.note: Extremely high birefringence — strongest of any common mineral.

physical.note: Based on chrysocolla / aquamarine analogue.

optical.note: Coal has relatively high IOR (1.6-1.8) but appears very dark due to extreme absorption.

surface.note: Bituminous coal can show vitreous (glassy) luster on fresh fracture surfaces.

physical.note: Coal doesn't melt — it decomposes/combusts. Flash point ~670K.

transmission.note: Standard window glass. Very slight green tint from iron impurities.

birefringence.note: Amorphous — no birefringence. Stress birefringence possible under load.

optical.note: Very low F0 — ice reflects only ~2% at normal incidence.

subsurface.note: Bulk ice appears blue because red light is absorbed preferentially over long path lengths.

transmission.note: Pure ice is transparent. Air bubbles and cracks cause opacity.

optical.note: Aggregate of feldspar (IOR 1.52-1.57), quartz (1.54), mica (1.56-1.60).
Dark color from carbonaceous material and iron sulfides.

surface.note: Porous texture. Higher roughness than crystalline stone.
Granular surface texture. Roughness depends on grain size and cementation.

optical.note: Red color from hematite (Fe2O3) grain coatings.
Dark color from pyroxene and olivine (high Fe/Mg silicates).

blackstone.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Dark basalt or gabbro

end_stone.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Pumice / Light tuff

physical.note: Based on pumice — porous, lightweight volcanic rock.

optical.note: Same mineral as calcite — deposited from solution.

subsurface.note: Translucent when thin. SSS similar to marble/calcite.

optical.note: Wood IOR varies 1.50-1.60. Cellulose IOR ~1.53, lignin ~1.61.

surface.anisotropy_note: Grain direction creates visible anisotropic reflection.

subsurface.note: Wood shows slight translucency in thin sections, especially lighter species.

coat.note: Natural wood has no coating. Varnished/lacquered wood: coat_weight=0.5-1.0, coat_ior=1.50, coat_roughness=0.05.

subsurface.note: Lighter color allows more visible subsurface scattering.

dark_oak_planks.real_world_material: Dark Oak / Bog Oak wood (Quercus robur aged)

subsurface.note: Dark wood absorbs more light — less visible SSS.

physical.note: Mangrove is notably dense — one of the denser tropical hardwoods.

surface.note: Cherry takes polish well — relatively smooth grain.

optical.note: Individual grains are quartz. Bulk reflectance is diffuse.

subsurface.note: Sand shows slight translucency at grain-to-grain contacts.

physical.note: Bulk density. Individual quartz grain density is 2650 kg/m3.

optical.note: Red color from hematite (Fe2O3) grain coatings.

subsurface.note: Wet clay shows noticeable translucency.

optical.note: Water saturation lowers effective IOR. Surface can show specular wetness.

coat.note: Wet surface film. Creates partial specular reflection over diffuse substrate.

optical.note: Effective IOR of bulk snow is lower than solid ice due to air gaps.

subsurface.note: Snow is a strong multiple scatterer. Blue tint emerges in deep snow (red absorption).

physical.note: Compacted snow density. Fresh powder ~100 kg/m3, glacial firn ~550-800.
Porous, lightweight. Based on diatomaceous earth.

netherrack.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Scoria / Vesicular basalt

physical.note: Porous volcanic rock analogue.

optical.note: Red color from iron oxide in fired clay.

nether_bricks.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Dark fired brick / clinker brick

optical.note: Over-fired brick analogue — darker color, denser, more vitrified.
Characteristic orange-red color from iron oxide.

surface.note: Glaze surface is very smooth — much lower roughness than unglazed.

coat.note: Glass-like glaze coating over the ceramic body.

wool.chemical_formula: Keratin protein (C + H + O + N + S)

optical.note: Keratin IOR ~1.54-1.56.

sheen.note: Wool fibers create a soft sheen at grazing angles.

subsurface.note: Fiber bundles allow light to scatter through.

physical.note: Bulk density including trapped air. Fiber density ~1300 kg/m3.

optical.note: Leaf wax cuticle IOR ~1.45-1.50. Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue, transmits green.

subsurface.note: Chlorophyll absorption: strong red (680nm) and blue (430nm) bands. Green channel transmits.

transmission.note: Thin leaves are noticeably translucent — backlit leaves glow green/yellow.

coat.note: Waxy cuticle coating on leaf surface.

physical.note: Block density (including air). Leaf tissue density ~700-1100 kg/m3.

optical.note: Aragonite polymorph of CaCO3. Higher IOR than calcite.

subsurface.note: Dead coral is white (pure CaCO3). Living coral colored by symbiotic algae.

physical.note: Dense coral skeleton. Porous coral much lighter.

subsurface.note: Mushroom flesh is highly translucent — strong subsurface scattering.
Porous structure allows significant internal light scattering.

physical.note: Dry sponge. Saturated sponge approaches water density.

surface.anisotropy_note: Hay bales have directional fiber alignment.

physical.note: Baled hay density. Individual straw fiber density ~500 kg/m3.

optical.note: Hydroxyapatite crystal IOR. Composite with collagen gives effective ~1.55-1.63.

subsurface.note: Thin bone sections are translucent — ivory shows strong SSS.

sculk.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Bioluminescent fungal biofilm

nether_wart_block.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Dense fungal tissue

crimson_nylium.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Mycelium-covered stone (red variant)

shroomlight.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Bioluminescent fungal fruiting body

subsurface.note: Warm bioluminescent glow permeates the entire block.

emission.note: Bright warm emitter — Minecraft light level 15.

subsurface.note: Beeswax is notably translucent — strong warm-toned SSS.
Outer rind is somewhat translucent (green). Flesh is highly translucent (red/pink).

physical.note: Mostly water (92%). High specific heat.

subsurface.note: Orange color from beta-carotene. Rind is somewhat translucent.

optical.note: Hematite IOR ~2.94 (very high for oxide). Not fully metallic — ore is oxide.

physical.note: Hematite density. Mixed ore is lower (~4000-5000).

raw_gold_block.real_world_material: Raw gold ore (native gold in quartz matrix)

complex_ior.note: Mix of gold metal and quartz. Effective F0 between gold (0.94) and quartz (0.046).

optical.note: Partially metallic — gold veins in quartz matrix.

physical.note: Lower density than pure gold — contains quartz gangue.

optical.note: Malachite IOR ~1.66-1.88. Not metallic — copper carbonate mineral.

subsurface.note: Malachite shows banded green translucency.

physical.note: Malachite analogue. Chalcopyrite is denser (~4200 kg/m3).

gilded_blackstone.real_world_material: Fictional — suggested analogue: Gold-veined dark basalt

optical.note: Mostly stone with metallic gold veins. Partial metalness.

complex_ior.source: Magnetite optical constants — Schlegel et al. 1979

optical.note: Semi-metallic oxide. High IOR but low k compared to true metals.

physical.note: Natural permanent magnet. The original 'magnet'.

surface.note: Calm water is a near-perfect mirror. Waves add roughness.

subsurface.note: Pure water absorption: red >> green >> blue. Blue color emerges over meters of path length.

transmission.note: Extremely transparent. Absorption only visible over long distances.

optical.note: Essentially molten glass. IOR similar to solid obsidian.

surface.note: Molten lava surface has moderate roughness from convection currents.

emission.color_note: Planckian blackbody at 1000-1200K: deep orange-red. Emissivity ~0.9 for rough molten rock.

physical.note: Basaltic lava. Viscosity varies enormously (10^2 to 10^10 Pa·s) with composition and temperature.

optical.note: IOR increases with sugar concentration. Typical honey ~1.49-1.51.

surface.note: Honey surface is very smooth and glossy.

subsurface.note: Honey is translucent with warm golden SSS.

transmission.note: Clear honey is quite transparent with golden tint.

physical.note: Viscosity varies enormously with temperature and water content.

optical.note: IOR between water (1.333) and polymer (1.50). Mostly water.

subsurface.note: Highly translucent green gel — strong SSS.

physical.note: Properties similar to water-based hydrogels.

optical.note: Mix of wood (1.55) and paper/cellulose (1.48). Averaged.

physical.note: Approximate — depends on book density.

crafting_table.real_world_material: Mixed — wood planks with tool marks

optical.note: TNT crystal IOR ~1.543. Block is wrapped in paper/canvas.
